# onetsolutions_hosting_redirect (Resource)

Manages a redirect of a web hosting, from a path of one of its domains to another URL.

~> **Destroying this resource only removes it from the state.** Terraform cannot remove a
redirect: it keeps working until it is removed in the web hosting's control panel, and the plan
warns about it. For the same reason a redirect cannot be changed in place: the plan refuses a new
`destination` or `type` for the same `domain` and `source` until the redirect in place is removed
in the control panel, and the resource stays in the state meanwhile. Changing the `domain` or the `source` adds a second redirect and
leaves the first one in place.

The web hosting must be active. Creating a redirect identical to one already in place (same
domain, source, destination and type) takes that one over instead of adding it twice. If the
redirect is removed outside Terraform, the next plan adds it again. Once the web hosting is
cancelled or terminated, the next refresh removes the redirect from the state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_web_hosting" "site" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_redirect" "old_page" {
  hosting_id  = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  domain      = "example.com"
  source      = "/old-page"
  destination = "https://example.com/new-page"
}

# Redirect a whole domain, temporarily.
resource "onetsolutions_hosting_redirect" "campaign" {
  hosting_id  = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  domain      = "promo.example.com"
  source      = "/"
  destination = "https://example.com/offers"
  type        = "302"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `destination` (String) The `http` or `https` URL to redirect to. A change fails while the previous redirect of this `source` is in place: remove it in the web hosting's control panel first (see the page's notes).
- `domain` (String) The domain of the web hosting the redirect applies to: its main domain, a subdomain or an addon domain, lowercase. Changing it adds another redirect and leaves the previous one in place.
- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting the redirect belongs to. Changing it recreates the redirect.
- `source` (String) The path to redirect, starting with `/`, such as `/old-page`; `/` redirects the whole domain. Changing it adds another redirect and leaves the previous one in place.

### Optional

- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `type` (String) `301` (permanent, the default) or `302` (temporary). A change fails while the previous redirect of this `source` is in place: remove it in the web hosting's control panel first (see the page's notes).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The domain followed by the source path, such as `example.com/old-page`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_redirect.old_page
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/example.com/old-page"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<domain>/<path>, or <hosting_id>/<domain>/<path> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_redirect.old_page 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/example.com/old-page
```
